note: Track legato (guitar-techniques), step 2: the trill with fingers 1 and 3 (legato-trill at level beginner) high on the neck, lower where the reach is wider, then on the B string. The intermediate copies (in stages, the legato warm-up) are folded in as an intermediate choice with the same words and a wider tempo range; the old Stage selector of tempos is now moves.

exercise.title: Hammer-ons and pull-offs, fingers 1 and 3
exercise.why: Fingers 1 and 3 have a fret between them, so finger 3 has further to fall than finger 2 did, and the trill trains it to land on its fret while finger 1 stays down.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}} and follow the tab. Pick the first note once, then hammer finger 3 on and pull it off, one note per beat, with no more picking. Finger 1 stays down the whole time.
Practice until both notes are equally loud.

Press Play below to start the metronome. The trill is now lower on the neck, where the frets are further apart, so finger 3 has to reach.
If finger 3 lands short of its fret, move your thumb along the back of the neck until it reaches.
_Stop and shake out your hand when it aches._

Press Play below to start the metronome and play the trill on the B string.
Practice until the trill is in your muscle memory: finger 3 lands and lifts without you thinking about it.
